summary: A dark, sci-fi-flavoured page for the revival and variable extension of Marvin (1969), made for Visions magazine: a scroll-driven hero where the headline grows heavier and smaller as it reveals more words, a weight-contrast word stack, a 2D-pad tester for weight × optical size, a full on-page Stripe checkout (Pro / Trial / Personal licences, per-weight pricing), commissioned postcards and posters, and two long designer essays on reviving and extending the face.

instances.look: On near-black, an all-caps headline in a red → pink → orange → yellow → cream gradient (one colour step per line). The first screen shows 'MARVIN / VISIONS / EXPANDS' as hairline caps filling the width; the stitched crop shows it getting bolder and smaller with each scroll step until the whole sentence 'MARVIN VISIONS EXPANDS & BECOMES A VARIABLE FONT WITH 2 OPTICAL SIZES & A RANGE OF WEIGHTS' fits, centred, in a heavy weight
instances.feel: Cinematic, like an opening title crawl
instances.ux: Scroll scrubs the headline: font-weight rises from ~20 to bold while font-size shrinks from 100% so further lines of the announcement come into view; the stage is pinned for ~5 viewports
instances.learn: Couple weight up with size down on scroll so the announcement literally 'expands' into its full sentence: the headline demonstrates the claim it makes

instances.variantDefinition: One editable sample beside a single two-dimensional pad: dragging one handle sets two axes at once (e.g. weight on one axis, optical size on the other), drawn as a crosshair in a square; unlike pointer-xy-axes, only the handle moves the type
instances.look: On off-white, three lines of editable caps 'TYPE YOUR OWN TEXT AND USE THE SLIDER TO CHANGE WEIGHTS & OPTICAL SIZES' at left, and at right a black ~300px square with thin white crosshair lines meeting at a white dot
instances.ux: Click the text to type; drag the dot inside the square: one direction changes font-weight, the other changes optical size (opsz 80–99), and the text size scales along with it
instances.learn: When two axes are coupled in practice (weight and optical size), give them one 2D handle instead of two sliders

The rest of the form is collapsed in the capture

instances.learn: One form for paid, trial and free: the licence choice drives which steps appear, and the word count of the licence ('390 words') invites people to read it
